title.meaning: Short name of the proposed investment or change, not the Jira story title.
title.impact: Lets portfolio leaders identify and compare demand without confusing an idea with an approved project.

type.meaning: Level of demand being considered; distinguish portfolio idea, independently managed project, and program.
type.example: Project — enhancement to an existing customer portal.
type.impact: Determines which governance and funding path is appropriate; several teams do not automatically make a program.

sponsor.meaning: Business executive or organization accountable for sponsoring the proposed investment.
sponsor.impact: Identifies who must justify value and seek initial funding approval.

value.meaning: Business problem or outcome expected, not a description of software screens.
value.example: Reduce agent-assisted vehicle changes by enabling eligible customers to self-serve.
value.impact: Enables business-value comparison and later benefits measurement.

priority.meaning: Relative urgency agreed in an intake process; avoid treating requester enthusiasm as a funded commitment.
priority.example: High — planned digital-servicing objective, subject to capacity review.
priority.impact: Supports sequencing against competing Okta, portal, and claims initiatives.

status.meaning: Current intake stage, rather than team sprint status.
status.example: Assessing; Approved for discovery; In delivery; Deferred.
status.impact: Distinguishes an idea under evaluation from one authorized for execution.

decision.meaning: Exact portfolio decision and rationale, with approval scope if known.
decision.example: Discovery funded; delivery authorization still requires an approved business case.
decision.impact: Prevents teams from treating preliminary exploration money as full-project approval.

metric.meaning: Specific benefit or guardrail that can be measured after release.
metric.example: Percentage of eligible vehicle-change transactions completed online.
metric.impact: Determines whether the new capability actually delivers business value.

baseline.meaning: Measured performance before the change; include units and observation period.
baseline.example: 0% digital Add/Replace Vehicle completions in the old portal.
baseline.impact: Without a credible starting point, improvement cannot be demonstrated.

target.meaning: Expected improvement by a defined date, agreed as a business hypothesis.
target.example: 40% of eligible changes completed online six months after launch.
target.impact: Supports benefit prioritization and release/rollout decisions; not a guaranteed outcome.

actual.meaning: Measured result to date using the same definition as baseline and target.
actual.example: 24% digital completion in the first post-release month.
actual.impact: Triggers adoption investigation or continued investment if benefits lag.

owner.meaning: Named person accountable for collecting and interpreting the business measure after project closure.
owner.example: Digital Product Owner for completion rate.
owner.impact: Prevents benefit measurement from ending when the temporary project closes.

measurement.meaning: Source, calculation, frequency and segment used to calculate the metric.
measurement.example: Monthly portal analytics: completed eligible transactions ÷ eligible attempts.
measurement.impact: Makes results reproducible and helps avoid misleading averages.

status.meaning: State of measurement or benefit realization, not code progress.
status.example: Baseline confirmed; Not measured; Improving; Off target.
status.impact: Shows whether evidence supports the investment case.

item.meaning: The specific charter element being approved or clarified.
item.example: In scope, Out of scope, Funding authority, Business objective.
item.impact: Organizes the agreement about what the project is and is not authorized to do.

detail.meaning: Clear, decision-ready statement of the charter element with boundaries.
detail.example: Replace Vehicle is included; standalone Remove Vehicle is excluded from initial launch.
detail.verify: Sponsor, Product Owner and subject-matter experts.
detail.impact: Avoids ambiguity when a new requirement is later proposed.

owner.meaning: Person who validates or approves this charter line, not necessarily its author.
owner.example: Sponsor for scope authority; PO for backlog details.
owner.impact: Shows where to obtain a binding answer before baseline approval.

status.meaning: Whether this charter element is drafted, validated, or approved.
status.example: Draft pending sponsor sign-off.
status.impact: Prevents an unapproved six-month target from being presented as a committed baseline.

name.meaning: Specific role, team or person the project depends on.
name.impact: Makes dependency and decision routing explicit.

role.meaning: Role played in the project, not simply a job title.
role.example: Portal Product Owner; enterprise IAM program lead.
role.impact: Separates product, Scrum, engineering, PM, and program responsibilities.

accountability.meaning: Outcome this stakeholder is responsible for delivering or assuring.
accountability.example: PolicyCenter lead owns endorsement API contract and readiness.
accountability.impact: Prevents unclear ownership when a milestone slips.

authority.meaning: Decisions the stakeholder can actually approve or escalate.
authority.example: Sponsor approves scope/date tradeoff; PO orders backlog within delegation.
authority.impact: Avoids sending budget or release decisions to people without approval rights.

engagement.meaning: How and when the PM should communicate with this stakeholder.
engagement.example: Weekly dependency review; monthly steering meeting.
engagement.impact: Sets a purposeful cadence rather than adding unnecessary ceremonies.

status.meaning: Current engagement or decision-readiness level.
status.example: Engaged; Awaiting confirmation; Escalation needed.
status.impact: Reveals absent decision-makers or commitment gaps.

milestone.meaning: Verifiable integrated delivery outcome across teams, not a sprint task.
milestone.example: PolicyCenter contract approved for Add/Replace transactions.
milestone.impact: Used to test whether the overall release forecast is credible.

owner.meaning: Single named lead accountable for evidence that this milestone is met.
owner.example: PolicyCenter technical lead for transaction API readiness.

baseline.meaning: Original approved milestone date retained for change history.
baseline.impact: Comparison point for variance; never silently overwrite after a slip.

forecast.meaning: Most recent credible completion date based on delivery evidence.
forecast.impact: Shows whether a delay moves SIT, UAT or production launch.

status.meaning: Current milestone condition based on evidence and agreed tolerances.
status.example: At risk because test endpoint has no confirmed date.
status.impact: Feeds project RAG and targeted management attention.

dependency.meaning: Specific upstream input that must arrive before milestone completion.
dependency.example: PolicyCenter endorsement API contract and test endpoint.
dependency.impact: Exposes the true constraint instead of assuming all teams can work independently.

evidence.meaning: Artifact, demonstration or approval proving milestone completion.
evidence.example: Signed API contract and successful portal contract-test results.
evidence.impact: Prevents optimistic progress reports based only on verbal assurances.

key.meaning: Unique identifier in Jira or the delivery backlog.
key.impact: Lets the PM trace integrated commitments to detailed delivery evidence.

type.meaning: Backlog hierarchy level used by this team; not every company uses identical Jira configuration.
type.impact: Prevents comparing a multi-sprint feature with a single story.

title.meaning: User- or system-facing capability expressed clearly enough to identify work.
title.example: Calculate revised premium when an insured vehicle is replaced.
title.impact: Connects sprint work to the customer journey and release scope.

owner.meaning: Person or team accountable for coordinating this backlog item; Jira assignee conventions vary.
owner.example: PolicyCenter lead for premium calculation feature.
owner.impact: Provides a contact for estimates, blockers and evidence.

pi.meaning: Planning Interval (PI) in which the feature is forecast or committed at ART level.
pi.impact: Aligns the feature with broader integrated planning, if the organization uses SAFe.

sprint.meaning: Iteration currently forecast for the work; this can change through team planning.
sprint.impact: Helps forecast feature readiness without directing the team’s Sprint Planning.

points.meaning: Team-relative story-point estimate; not a universal measure of hours or performance.
points.example: 8 points estimated by the team for a feature slice.
points.impact: Provides local forecasting input; never add points across unrelated teams as standardized effort.

status.meaning: Current workflow state in the team’s configured Jira process.
status.example: Ready, In progress, Blocked, In review, Done.
status.impact: Shows delivery progress, but Done stories alone do not prove the release is ready.

acceptance.meaning: Testable condition that demonstrates the intended capability works.
acceptance.example: Replacement premium and effective date agree with PolicyCenter policy record.
acceptance.impact: Links requirements to demonstrable, accepted functionality.

iteration.meaning: Sprint or PI identifier, using the team’s actual cadence and calendar.
iteration.example: S4, or PI-1 for a multi-sprint planning interval.
iteration.impact: Keeps team commitments separate from project milestone governance.

goal.meaning: Outcome the team intends to demonstrate, not merely a count of tickets.
goal.example: Customer can review premium impact for a replacement vehicle.
goal.impact: Connects iteration progress to a meaningful capability.

capacity.meaning: Team's expected ability to complete work in relative planning points during the sprint or PI (not resource person-days). Use consistent team-specific point conventions.
capacity.example: S4 forecast capacity: 38 relative points, while the current plan requests 40. That is an overcommitment to review.
capacity.verify: Scrum Developers, Product Owner and Scrum Master.
capacity.impact: Comparing sprint planned points against empirical team capacity helps identify an unrealistic commitment. Never compare points against another team's person-days.

planned.meaning: Relative point estimate for work selected or planned for the sprint or PI; not a time or cost unit.
planned.example: S4 team has selected 40 points against a 38-point forecast capacity.
planned.impact: Shows potential overcommitment. Individual story-level records in the demo are illustrative samples, not a complete backlog roll-up.

done.meaning: Relative point total for work meeting the team's Definition of Done by the stated snapshot. Completed sprints can deliver fewer points than planned.
done.example: S1 planned 34 points and completed 30; the remaining work is re-evaluated for later planning.
done.verify: Scrum team / delivery evidence in Jira.
done.impact: Keeps sprint status and PI rollups honest; not a measure of cross-team productivity.

confidence.meaning: Qualitative assessment of ability to meet the iteration or PI objective, backed by risks.
confidence.example: Low because PolicyCenter API is not ready.
confidence.verify: Teams during planning and risk review.
confidence.impact: Signals where management must remove cross-team obstacles.

demo.meaning: Specific working behavior to show stakeholders in the review/system demo.
demo.example: Replace Vehicle journey displays the PolicyCenter premium response.
demo.impact: Provides evidence of integrated outcomes rather than slide-only progress.

status.meaning: Lifecycle stage of the iteration objective.
status.example: Planning, In progress, Achieved, Partially achieved.
status.impact: Allows inspection and learning without turning the PM into the Scrum Master.

deliverable.meaning: Exact upstream item another team must provide; avoid a vague label like “API dependency”.
deliverable.example: Working PolicyCenter endorsement endpoint in the test environment.
deliverable.impact: Defines what “ready” means for the handoff.

producer.meaning: Team responsible for providing the deliverable.
producer.impact: Identifies who can make and fulfill the commitment.

consumer.meaning: Team or workstream that cannot proceed without the deliverable.
consumer.impact: Shows where slippage creates downstream impact.

neededBy.meaning: Last date the consuming team needs the input to protect its plan.
neededBy.impact: Key date for assessing schedule exposure.

forecast.meaning: Producer’s latest evidence-backed delivery date, separate from the consuming need date.
forecast.impact: If after needed-by, trigger impact analysis and recovery options.

impact.meaning: Concrete consequence if the dependency misses its need date.
impact.example: SIT start moves seven calendar days; release forecast needs revalidation.
impact.impact: Used to prioritize escalations and make tradeoffs visible.

owner.meaning: Person accountable for tracking and resolving this dependency through agreed channels.
owner.example: PolicyCenter delivery lead with portal PM coordinating.
owner.impact: Keeps the entry actionable; coordination ownership is not coding ownership.

status.meaning: Current readiness and commitment condition.
status.example: At risk — API contract agreed but endpoint not deployed.
status.impact: Distinguishes a confirmed blocker from a possible late delivery.

escalate.meaning: Date to raise unresolved risk before the dependency actually blocks the plan.
escalate.impact: Provides time for staffing, sequencing or governance decisions.

team.meaning: Delivery team or skill pool whose capacity is being forecast.
team.example: Portal QA team, PolicyCenter integration specialists.
team.impact: Identifies the source of capacity and possible shared allocations.

skill.meaning: Specialized capability required; headcount alone can hide shortages.
skill.example: Guidewire endorsement integration or E2E test automation.
skill.impact: Shows why spare frontend capacity cannot replace an unavailable PC specialist.

people.meaning: Number of people available in this planning period, adjusted for actual allocation if necessary.
people.example: 4 QA engineers assigned to portal work.
people.impact: Starting point for available person-day calculation; do not double-count shared people.

daysPerPerson.meaning: Working days per person in this calculation period before specific leave/support deductions.
daysPerPerson.impact: Defines the period and unit; do not mix weeks, hours and person-days.

leave.meaning: Person-days lost to PTO, holidays, or known absences across the team.
leave.example: 4 person-days of leave for the portal QA team.
leave.impact: Reduces delivery capacity; do not subtract a holiday twice.

support.meaning: Person-days reserved for production incidents, operations and ongoing portal maintenance.
support.example: 8 QA person-days reserved for production support.
support.impact: Protects BAU commitments instead of promising all capacity to new features.

other.meaning: Person-days committed to other initiatives, learning or non-feature duties not already deducted.
other.example: 6 QA person-days for enterprise Okta regression testing.
other.impact: Makes competing enterprise assignments visible in release forecasting.

available.meaning: Read-only calculated person-days for the team: people × working days each − leave − support − other allocated commitments.
available.example: Portal QA 4 × 10 − 4 leave − 8 support − 6 other (including Okta) = 22 person-days.
available.impact: Never manually type this derivative; update the staffing and allocation inputs to change available capacity.

owner.meaning: Leader who confirms allocation and resolves staffing decisions within authority.
owner.example: QA Manager for portal QA resources.
owner.impact: Identifies who can commit capacity; PM does not automatically control staffing.

category.meaning: Cost component or ring-fenced reserve being forecast.
category.example: Portal delivery; PolicyCenter integration; Contingency reserve.
category.impact: Allows cost drivers and protected contingency to be distinguished.

baseline.meaning: Approved cost allowance for this category, using the same currency and period.
baseline.example: $420,000 for portal delivery over the planned project.
baseline.impact: Reference against which forecast variance is calculated.

actual.meaning: Cost recognized/spent to date, reconciled with Finance; not cash remaining.
actual.example: $90,000 charged to portal delivery through the reporting cutoff.
actual.impact: Helps calculate estimate at completion and assess burn rate.

etc.meaning: Estimate to complete: realistic remaining cost including future labor and vendor work.
etc.impact: EAC = actual + ETC; do not treat ETC as approved remaining budget.

commitments.meaning: Signed or otherwise obligated future costs that are already included inside the estimate to complete, not an additional EAC component.
commitments.example: $10,000 future vendor obligation within the $320,000 remaining portal-delivery forecast.
commitments.verify: Finance, Procurement and accountable delivery lead.
commitments.impact: Check unfunded commitments and avoid double counting by adding commitments to actual + ETC.

owner.meaning: Manager accountable for providing the cost forecast for this line.
owner.impact: Ensures the PM can validate estimates and seek approvals.

id.meaning: Stable identifier used across status reports and decision logs.
id.example: R-002 for potential Okta/portal QA capacity conflict.
id.impact: Allows traceability and avoids duplicate risk entries.

type.meaning: Choose Risk, Assumption, Issue or Dependency based on present facts.
type.example: Risk: Okta may reduce portal QA capacity; Issue: staff already reassigned.
type.impact: Determines whether to mitigate likelihood, validate, resolve, or manage a handoff.

description.meaning: Objective statement describing trigger or event and consequence; avoid generic “integration risk”.
description.example: PolicyCenter endpoint may slip beyond the SIT start date.
description.impact: Makes the problem testable and actionable.

impact.meaning: Consequence severity on schedule, cost, quality, customer or controls; use your organization’s scale.
impact.example: High because a delayed endorsement API blocks integrated test exit.
impact.impact: Drives escalation and prioritization based on project tolerances.

likelihood.meaning: Estimated probability of a future risk; not applicable to issues that already occurred.
likelihood.example: High after repeated missed API readiness checkpoints.
likelihood.impact: Supports mitigation focus; avoid false numerical precision.

owner.meaning: Single person accountable for mitigation or resolution, even if others perform the work.
owner.impact: Prevents risks from sitting unowned in the log.

due.meaning: Date by which the next mitigation action or evidence is expected.
due.impact: Allows action follow-up before a release milestone is missed.

mitigation.meaning: Practical action that reduces probability or impact, with accountable follow-up.
mitigation.example: Agree API contract early and schedule contract testing before full SIT.
mitigation.impact: Produces a recovery path instead of mere RAG reporting.

status.meaning: Open, Monitoring, Mitigated, Resolved, Closed or another organization-defined state.
status.example: Open — confirmation pending from PolicyCenter.
status.impact: Distinguishes ongoing exposure from a closed item supported by evidence.

id.meaning: Unique change-control reference linked to approvals and roadmap history.
id.impact: Supports traceability across the charter, plan and budget.

request.meaning: Requested modification to scope, baseline cost, date or acceptance approach.
request.example: Include standalone Remove Vehicle in the initial release.
request.impact: Identifies whether this is backlog reprioritization or a material baseline change.

impact.meaning: Summary of cross-functional scope, cost, technical, schedule, testing and compliance consequences.
impact.example: Requires new PolicyCenter rules, two E2E paths and additional UAT.
impact.impact: Provides decision-quality tradeoffs instead of approval by enthusiasm.

cost.meaning: Incremental forecast cost of the change; use currency and clearly distinguish cost from savings.
cost.impact: Determines whether delegated funding thresholds are exceeded.

days.meaning: Estimated movement to the integrated milestone or release, not raw work effort.
days.example: 21 calendar days added to release forecast if scope is retained.

sponsor.meaning: Business owner/requester advocating the change; not necessarily the financial approver.

decision.meaning: Formal disposition and reason from authorized governance.
decision.example: Deferred to a subsequent release after impact review.
decision.impact: Ensures approved changes are reflected in plan and finance.

status.meaning: Current stage of change analysis and approval.
status.example: Pending analysis; Submitted; Approved; Rejected.
status.impact: Prevents implementing material changes without authorization.

id.meaning: Stable decision reference for governance, risks and meeting minutes.
id.impact: Links the final approval to the issue it resolves.

question.meaning: Precisely worded decision someone with authority must make.
question.example: Do we retain launch date if the Replace Vehicle API slips three weeks?
question.impact: Focuses governance on a yes/no or explicit option choice.

options.meaning: Feasible alternatives with clear scope, date, cost and risk consequences.
options.example: Resequence tests; split Add/Replace release; extend launch.
options.impact: Prevents one-sided escalation without meaningful alternatives.

recommendation.meaning: PM’s supported recommendation and assumptions; do not present as already approved.
recommendation.example: Run an API spike, then choose scoped release if integration still slips.
recommendation.impact: Lets the authority decide with evidence rather than accept a vague blocker.

authority.meaning: Person or forum with delegated power to make the decision.
authority.example: Business Sponsor for scope/date tradeoff; Release Authority for Go/No-Go.
authority.impact: Prevents accidental approval by the wrong participant.

due.meaning: Latest date the decision can be made without causing additional impact.
due.example: 2027-03-03 before QA test window is lost.
due.impact: Identifies urgent decisions before the situation becomes irreversible.

decision.meaning: Actual approved choice and any conditions, not merely what PM recommended.
decision.example: Approve Add Vehicle first; Replace Vehicle follows after controls pass.
decision.impact: Becomes authoritative input to scope, roadmap and release plan.

status.meaning: Decision lifecycle: Requested, Pending, Approved, Rejected, Closed.
status.example: Pending sponsor review.
status.impact: Shows outstanding governance debt and aging approvals.

scenario.meaning: Insurance journey or control being validated; not simply a test-case count.
scenario.example: Replace Vehicle with future effective date and premium adjustment.
scenario.impact: Shows test coverage for business-critical behavior.

level.meaning: Type of testing used for this record.
level.example: E2E for portal → PolicyCenter → confirmation; UAT for business acceptance.
level.impact: Ensures technical and business validation are not conflated.

owner.meaning: Accountable lead for execution/evidence; not the Project Manager automatically.
owner.example: QA Lead for E2E; Business Lead for UAT.
owner.impact: Provides a clear source for readiness reporting.

planned.meaning: Number of planned scenarios/cases in this test slice with a defined counting method.
planned.impact: Denominator for interpreting progress and remaining exposure.

passed.meaning: Number that ran successfully with recorded evidence.
passed.example: 16 cases passed in the integrated environment.
passed.impact: Shows demonstrated coverage, not just attempted execution.

failed.meaning: Number executed with an unmet expected result.
failed.example: 2 failures caused by incorrect premium effective date.
failed.impact: Feeds severity, re-test demand and release risk.

blocked.meaning: Number that cannot execute because prerequisite, data or environment is missing.
blocked.impact: Exposes external constraints affecting test exit.

status.meaning: Quality readiness condition for this slice based on exit criteria.
status.example: At risk — 2 blocked scenarios and one unresolved high-severity defect.
status.verify: QA Lead and business as applicable.
status.impact: Informs release readiness without having PM override QA judgment.

evidence.meaning: Link or reference to the test execution summary, defects and approvals.
evidence.example: Jira test run, defect IDs and PolicyCenter transaction trace.
evidence.impact: Allows sponsor/release authority to verify quality claims.

gate.meaning: Specific readiness condition to be satisfied before deployment/customer exposure.
gate.example: E2E exit criteria achieved and critical defects dispositioned.

owner.meaning: Lead responsible for producing the readiness evidence.
owner.example: QA Lead for E2E sign-off; Service Owner for monitoring readiness.
owner.impact: Separates test execution, operational readiness and PM coordination.

evidence.meaning: Document, test result or runbook proving the gate was met.
evidence.example: QA completion report with outstanding defect disposition.

due.meaning: Date readiness evidence must be available before the Go/No-Go meeting.
due.example: 2027-06-11 for UAT sign-off ahead of release.
due.impact: Protects time for review and remediation.

status.meaning: Gate state, including explicit exceptions where allowed.
status.example: Not started, In review, Passed, Exception approved.
status.impact: Controls whether release recommendation is supported.

approver.meaning: Actual authority that accepts this gate or grants an exception.
approver.example: Security Lead for security finding; Release Authority for final release.
approver.impact: Prevents PM from unilaterally accepting high-risk release conditions.

item.meaning: Service readiness or hypercare condition that must be tracked.
item.example: Failed policy transaction rate during initial launch.
item.impact: Defines safe production operation after deployment.

owner.meaning: Operational person accountable for monitoring and response.
owner.example: Service Owner, incident commander or PolicyCenter operations lead.
owner.impact: Ensures support is not left with the temporary project team indefinitely.

threshold.meaning: Agreed measurable exit or alert criterion, with unit and window.
threshold.example: Failed policy transactions below 2% for an agreed monitoring period.
threshold.impact: Makes hypercare exit based on service stability rather than calendar alone.

actual.meaning: Current observed operational measurement from monitoring or incident records.
actual.example: 1.1% failed transactions over the last 24 hours.
actual.impact: Determines whether rollout should expand, pause or recover.

status.meaning: Readiness, active monitoring or exit status.
status.example: Monitoring; Threshold breached; Handover accepted.
status.impact: Provides visible accountability for support transition.

evidence.meaning: Dashboard, incident review or signed handover supporting the status.
evidence.example: Production telemetry link and reconciled failed-transaction report.

vendor.meaning: External company or provider with a documented delivery obligation.
vendor.impact: Identifies the contractual counterparty, not an informal internal team.

deliverable.meaning: Specific product/service the provider must deliver and acceptance criteria.
deliverable.example: Integration support package and test evidence for contract milestone.
deliverable.impact: Lets PM compare promised work to actual acceptance evidence.

contract.meaning: SOW, purchase order or service agreement governing the obligation.
contract.impact: Connects schedule and scope decisions to commercial terms.

due.meaning: Contractual or negotiated date for a deliverable.
due.impact: Allows timely escalation and impact analysis.

owner.meaning: Internal person accountable for vendor relationship and acceptance coordination.
owner.example: Vendor Manager with architect verifying technical outputs.
owner.impact: Avoids treating the Project Manager as automatic legal contract owner.

status.meaning: Current contractual/delivery condition.
status.example: On track, Awaiting acceptance, Delayed, Disputed.
status.impact: Exposes commercial or acceptance blockers.

escalation.meaning: Named governance/contact path and time limit for unresolved delivery problems.
escalation.example: Escalate missed SOW milestone to vendor account lead within two business days.
escalation.impact: Provides a usable resolution path before cross-project delivery is affected.

control.meaning: Business, security, legal or technical safeguard requiring verification.
control.example: Only authorized policyholders can submit a vehicle endorsement.
control.impact: Defines what risk must be controlled, not a generic “compliance done” checkbox.

evidence.meaning: Test results, policy rules, audit logs or approved assessment proving the control works.
evidence.example: Okta access test evidence and PolicyCenter audit trail.
evidence.impact: Gives release authority evidence for acceptance or exception.

owner.meaning: Named person responsible for verifying the control.
owner.example: Security Lead for access control; underwriting SME for eligibility.
owner.impact: Ensures proper specialists interpret applicable requirements.

status.meaning: Review, test and remediation condition.
status.example: Open pending state eligibility review; Verified after test sign-off.
status.impact: Flags release blockers and unverified assumptions.

approval.meaning: Recorded approval or exception from the authorized control owner.
approval.example: Security approval ID SEC-114; conditional exception with expiry.
approval.impact: Prevents unsupported claims of regulatory or security clearance.

period.meaning: Reporting interval and as-of date; avoid mixing observations from different periods.
period.impact: Makes trends and forecasts comparable week to week.

overall.meaning: Integrated project health against agreed tolerance, not average sprint colors.
overall.example: Amber: PC integration threatens planned SIT date.

schedule.meaning: Assessment of approved milestone dates against current forecast.
schedule.example: Red if release will miss baseline beyond agreed tolerance.
schedule.impact: Makes schedule exposure transparent independent of team velocity.

budget.meaning: Cost forecast versus approved authority, considering ETC and commitments.
budget.example: Amber if EAC threatens contingency or approval threshold.
budget.impact: Warns of future overrun even if current spend is low.

scope.meaning: Confidence that approved must-have functionality remains deliverable and controlled.
scope.example: Green if Add/Replace scope unchanged; Amber if removal feature threatens scope.
scope.impact: Identifies uncontrolled expansion or threatened benefits.

quality.meaning: Readiness trend from testing, defects, control outcomes and operational evidence.
quality.example: Amber when E2E scenarios remain blocked by PC endpoint.
quality.impact: Shows quality exposure, not a cosmetic test-completion percentage.

narrative.meaning: Two- or three-sentence executive assessment of cause, impact and current action.
narrative.example: Portal sprint delivery on plan; PC endpoint slips one week, threatening SIT; impact assessment underway.
narrative.verify: PM based on verified lead inputs.
narrative.impact: Explains why RAG changed and what leadership should expect next.

decisionNeeded.meaning: Exact action or choice requiring authority, with owner and required-by date.
decisionNeeded.example: Sponsor to choose phased release versus date extension by March 8.
decisionNeeded.impact: Turns the weekly status report into an actionable leadership tool.

action.meaning: Concrete diagnostic or stabilization step to restore a credible delivery forecast.
action.example: Reassess integrated test readiness rather than counting completed stories.
action.impact: Moves recovery from blame to verified facts and options.

owner.meaning: Person accountable for finishing the recovery action.
owner.example: PM + QA Lead for integrated-state assessment.
owner.impact: Prevents recovery tasks from becoming unassigned suggestions.

due.meaning: Decision or completion deadline for the recovery action.
due.impact: Supports short checkpoints and timely sponsor intervention.

status.meaning: Current progress and acceptance of the recovery action.
status.example: Open; In progress; Evidence reviewed; Complete.
status.impact: Helps measure whether the recovery plan is actually being executed.

evidence.meaning: Objective proof of completed assessment or recovery.
evidence.example: Updated integrated forecast with confirmed PC endpoint date and test impact.
evidence.impact: Avoids relabeling a Red project Green without real improvement.

initiative.meaning: Separately governed project or workstream coordinated within the wider business objective.
initiative.example: Add/Replace Vehicle portal project; related enterprise Okta rollout.
initiative.impact: Shows program scope without treating every dependent team as a program.

manager.meaning: Lead responsible for this initiative’s own delivery commitments.
manager.impact: Makes escalations go through appropriate project leadership.

businessValue.meaning: Benefit the initiative contributes to the broader program, expressed as a business outcome.
businessValue.impact: Keeps program coordination focused on benefits rather than project count.

baseline.meaning: Approved milestone/release date at initiative level.

forecast.meaning: Latest integrated forecast provided by the accountable project lead.

status.meaning: Health of the initiative as agreed in governance.
status.example: Amber due to unresolved shared PolicyCenter dependency.
status.impact: Shows where program-level intervention is needed.

sharedDependency.meaning: Resource, technical service, vendor or decision that affects multiple initiatives.
sharedDependency.example: Shared IAM test window across portal and enterprise Okta rollout.
sharedDependency.impact: Justifies program-level priority and capacity coordination.

relationship.meaning: Whether the initiative is a confirmed member, potential related project, outside enterprise dependency, or separate portfolio idea.
relationship.example: Enterprise Okta rollout is an external enterprise program: it affects portal testing but does not automatically join the portal servicing program.
relationship.verify: Program Sponsor, Portfolio leadership and initiative owners.
relationship.impact: Prevents combining unrelated project budgets and benefits or misrepresenting a group of initiatives as an approved program.

epic.meaning: Potential major portfolio investment or change initiative; not necessarily a Jira user story.
epic.impact: Item to analyze in portfolio Kanban and compare against available investment capacity.

valueStream.meaning: Persistent end-to-end business or development flow that the investment enables.
valueStream.impact: Connects investment to long-lived teams and outcomes rather than temporary departments.

businessValue.meaning: Relative business value score agreed using consistent local criteria.
businessValue.example: 8 on a 1–10 relative scale for improved customer servicing.
businessValue.impact: One component of WSJF; not a dollar forecast or automatic investment approval.

timeCriticality.meaning: Relative cost of delaying this investment or missing a window.
timeCriticality.example: 9 where regulatory or seasonal timing is important.
timeCriticality.impact: Contributes to Cost of Delay component of WSJF.

riskReduction.meaning: Relative reduction in risk or creation of future opportunity.
riskReduction.example: 7 where modernization retires a fragile integration.
riskReduction.impact: Represents Risk Reduction/Opportunity Enablement in WSJF.

jobSize.meaning: Relative effort or duration compared with other epics scored using the same approach.
jobSize.example: 5 for a small initiative; 13 for a larger one.
jobSize.impact: WSJF denominator; smaller size raises priority when other values are equal.

status.meaning: Portfolio Kanban state and authorization stage.
status.example: Review; Analyzing; Implementing; Done.
status.impact: Prevents early-stage epic scores being mistaken for approved funding.

decision.meaning: Explicit investment or capacity choice, with named authority and conditions.
decision.example: Approved for discovery only, pending estimates and capacity review.
decision.impact: Records why an epic was selected, deferred or stopped.

stage.meaning: One real step in the customer-to-outcome flow; avoid grouping whole departments as stages.
stage.example: Eligibility lookup before Add Vehicle submission.

workingDays.meaning: Total active processing time for this stage of the illustrative CURRENT assisted vehicle-servicing workflow, in equivalent 8-hour business days.
workingDays.example: Agent intake 0.0375 business-day ≈ 18 minutes of active work, while other back-office stages also consume work time.
workingDays.verify: Operations SMEs and actual process time study.
workingDays.impact: Do not confuse total end-to-end active time with a single agent's handling time or with the future self-service flow.

waitingDays.meaning: Queue or elapsed waiting time in 8-hour business-day equivalents for the current assisted process, without double-counting active work.
waitingDays.example: A back-office eligibility queue may add 1.5 business days even though lookup work takes minutes.
waitingDays.impact: Creates a useful process baseline; the future self-service outcome should reduce customer waiting and exceptions.

owner.meaning: Business or service owner responsible for the stage’s operating result.
owner.example: Policy Services owner for eligibility lookup.
owner.impact: Identifies who can improve the bottleneck across functional boundaries.

bottleneck.meaning: Observed constraint causing wait, rework or failures, supported by evidence.
bottleneck.example: Backend rating request queues while account eligibility is checked.
bottleneck.impact: Focuses improvement investment on actual flow constraints.

improvement.meaning: Proposed measurable change to eliminate or reduce the constraint.
improvement.example: Prevalidate eligibility before requesting a premium quote.
improvement.impact: Creates a testable hypothesis for cycle-time improvement.

audience.meaning: Group whose day-to-day behavior changes when the new capability or operating model launches.
audience.example: Customer service agents handling exceptions after self-service rollout.
audience.impact: Defines who needs communication and support.

change.meaning: Specific process, role or decision behavior expected to change.
change.example: Agents handle exceptions rather than routine add-vehicle requests.
change.impact: Prevents transformation from being described only as software deployment.

owner.meaning: Person accountable for adoption within this affected group.
owner.impact: Creates ownership beyond sending a training email.

communication.meaning: Channel, timing and content explaining what changes and why.
communication.example: Service bulletin and supervisor briefings two weeks before launch.

training.meaning: Concrete enablement activity tied to changed tasks.
training.example: Hands-on walkthrough for a failed endorsement and assisted recovery.
training.impact: Reduces operational risk and makes training relevant.

adoption.meaning: Actual usage or observed behavioral measure—not only training attendance.
adoption.example: 80% of eligible agents use the new exception workflow after four weeks.
adoption.impact: Provides evidence that the operating model is adopted.

status.meaning: Readiness and adoption progress for the audience.
status.example: Planning, Piloting, At risk, Adopted.
status.impact: Indicates intervention needs before and after launch.

deliverable.meaning: Formal closure condition or handover artifact that must be completed.
deliverable.example: Operational handover accepted by the named service owner.
deliverable.impact: Prevents premature project closure after code deployment.

owner.meaning: Person responsible for providing closure evidence or accepting transition.
owner.example: Finance for final cost; Service Owner for production handover.

acceptance.meaning: Definition of done or sign-off required for this closure item.
acceptance.example: No critical incidents and signed runbook acceptance.

status.meaning: Current state of the closure action.
status.example: Pending, Awaiting approval, Complete.
status.impact: Makes remaining handover or contract obligations visible.

evidence.meaning: Document/reference showing the closure condition is satisfied.
evidence.example: Approved closeout report, final cost reconciliation, signed support handover.
evidence.impact: Supports auditability and future lessons learned.

industry.meaning: Industry context used to adapt the training scenario.
industry.impact: The same delivery practices can be adapted to healthcare, banking or other industries.

case.meaning: Name of the active sample initiative, independent of the portal product name.
case.impact: Provides context for the registers and examples.

portfolio.meaning: Strategic grouping within which this project or program is considered.
portfolio.impact: Helps connect work to investment and priority decisions.

projectStart.meaning: Planning start date of the initiative; not necessarily first coding sprint.
projectStart.impact: Reference for integrated schedule and staffing.

targetRelease.meaning: Proposed customer release date; clarify whether approved baseline or preliminary target.
targetRelease.impact: Used to test schedule and dependency consequences.

budget.meaning: Read-only total authorized financial baseline, derived from every financial register baseline including contingency reserve.
budget.example: $1,050,000 approved base estimate plus $150,000 reserve equals $1,200,000 authorization.
budget.impact: Edit baseline cost lines in Budget & Forecast; this setting updates automatically to prevent mismatch.

asOfDate.meaning: The scenario snapshot date to which completed milestones, spending, sprint status and risk reporting refer. This may be a future fictional date in training.
asOfDate.example: 2027-02-19: a fictional Week 7 progress snapshot. The case began Jan 4 and the charter was approved Jan 15.
asOfDate.verify: Scenario facilitator / Project Manager; Finance for actual-as-of costs.
asOfDate.impact: Prevents claiming actual spending or completed deliverables before their dates; overdue checks use this value.

overallHealth.meaning: Integrated Red/Amber/Green assessment from the latest executive status record; not calculated by averaging team sprints.
overallHealth.example: Amber: PolicyCenter API readiness threatens the integrated test milestone.
overallHealth.impact: Prompts leadership attention to schedule, quality, scope, financial and dependency exposure.

milestoneCompletion.meaning: Count of integrated milestones whose recorded status is completed divided by all scheduled milestones.
milestoneCompletion.impact: Prevents confusing Jira story velocity with integrated delivery readiness.

eacOverview.meaning: Estimated total project cost at completion (EAC = actual + ETC), compared with both the base plan and total authorization including the separate reserve.
eacOverview.example: $220k actual + $845k ETC = $1.065M; $15k above $1.05M base, $135k below the $1.2M authorization.
eacOverview.verify: Finance and workstream owners; confirm remaining contracts are included within ETC.
eacOverview.impact: The difference below total authorization is unused contingency, not necessarily cost savings. Reserve use needs governance.

openWatch.meaning: Count only external dependencies genuinely at risk or forecast past their needed-by date. Open RAID entries are shown separately and may describe the same underlying problem.
openWatch.example: PolicyCenter API needed March 1, forecast March 8; counted as at risk. Okta planning marked Open but still on time is not automatically at risk.
openWatch.verify: Project Manager and producing delivery leads.
openWatch.impact: Avoid overstating project risk by treating every open item as a missed dependency or adding duplicate register counts.

approvedBaseline.meaning: Sum of approved cost-category baselines in the financial register.
approvedBaseline.impact: Compare it with forecast end cost; do not mistake the metadata budget for the detailed register.

actualCost.meaning: Posted/invoiced costs incurred up to the reporting cutoff, as entered in the financial register.
actualCost.example: $500,000 actuals booked through the current period.
actualCost.impact: Makes spending visible, but alone does not show whether the project will finish within budget.

estimateToComplete.meaning: Current cost forecast for work not yet completed.
estimateToComplete.example: $800,000 expected to finish integration, testing and deployment.
estimateToComplete.impact: Reforecast remaining work after scope, vendor, staffing or schedule changes.

costVariance.meaning: Cost forecast minus total authorized baseline, including contingency; a negative value means forecast below authorization, not necessarily under base budget.
costVariance.example: $1.065M EAC − $1.2M authorization = −$135k; forecast reserve draw against $1.05M base is $15k.
costVariance.verify: Finance / PMO; validate scope and cost-to-complete.
costVariance.impact: Use both base and authorized comparisons to judge reserve consumption rather than prematurely claiming realized savings.

usableDays.meaning: Sum of capacity person-days across the listed skill groups. This aggregate is not interchangeable capacity; each specialty has distinct work and commitments.
usableDays.example: 50 developer + 22 QA + 12 PolicyCenter + 8 business SME = 92 nonfungible person-days in the two-week window.
usableDays.impact: You cannot allocate all 92 days to development; evaluate skills and independently committed time.

assignedPeople.meaning: Total people entered on team-capacity lines, not necessarily unique individuals or full-time equivalents.
assignedPeople.example: 8 portal developers plus 4 portal QA engineers.
assignedPeople.impact: Use skill and allocation detail rather than treating raw headcount as productivity.

supportDays.meaning: Team person-days reserved to keep live customer portal operations running.
supportDays.example: 8 QA days reserved for production defects and regressions during the sprint.
supportDays.impact: Prevents promising full-team capacity to Add/Replace Vehicle while production continues.

nonFeatureDays.meaning: Total team person-days reserved for leave and other activities, such as Okta integration work.
nonFeatureDays.example: 4 QA leave days plus 6 Okta regression days.
nonFeatureDays.impact: Avoid double subtraction when the same activity is recorded in another category.

plannedTests.meaning: Aggregate planned test cases across recorded QA scenarios; only meaningful if all rows use the same counting basis.
plannedTests.impact: Tracks expected coverage; does not by itself indicate readiness.

passedTests.meaning: QA executions recorded as passed on the tested build/environment.
passedTests.example: 18 passed E2E cases with Guidewire policy transaction checks.
passedTests.impact: Use associated defect and backend evidence before claiming functional readiness.

failedTests.meaning: Executions with a deviation from expected results.
failedTests.example: 2 tests fail because policy effective date is incorrect.
failedTests.verify: QA Lead and engineering defect owners
failedTests.impact: A single critical failure may block release regardless of overall pass rate.

blockedTests.meaning: Test cases unable to run because of missing data, environment, credentials or dependent functionality.
blockedTests.example: 3 E2E tests waiting for a PolicyCenter test endpoint.
blockedTests.impact: Make the external dependency and unblock date explicit.

workingTime.meaning: Sum of active processing time across the modeled value stream steps, expressed in elapsed days.
workingTime.example: 0.02 days to process policy eligibility lookup.
workingTime.impact: Compare actual work time with waiting time; this is not a staff-effort total.

waitingTime.meaning: Sum of elapsed time between work steps, including handoff queues and approvals.
waitingTime.example: 1.5 days waiting for an external policy service response.
waitingTime.impact: Often reveals bottlenecks that sprint velocity does not capture.

elapsedTime.meaning: Total modeled lead time: working time plus waiting time.
elapsedTime.example: 2.0 working days + 5.0 waiting days = 7.0 days end-to-end.
elapsedTime.impact: Use a consistent start and end boundary when comparing changes.

flowEfficiency.meaning: Working time divided by total elapsed time, expressed as a percentage.
flowEfficiency.example: 2 working days / 7 elapsed days = 28.6% flow efficiency.
flowEfficiency.impact: Shows where queue reduction might matter more than individual team throughput.

activity.meaning: Work or decision covered by this assignment.
activity.impact: Clarifies the handoff and escalation path.

responsible.meaning: People who carry out the work or prepare the decision.
responsible.impact: Clarifies the handoff and escalation path.

accountable.meaning: One person who owns the outcome or makes the decision.
accountable.impact: Clarifies the handoff and escalation path.

consulted.meaning: People who provide input before the decision.
consulted.impact: Clarifies the handoff and escalation path.

informed.meaning: People who receive the outcome or status update.
informed.impact: Clarifies the handoff and escalation path.
